summary: HSF draw owner. Recorded to carry the consumer half of a cross-translation-unit retail invariant: FaceDraw's && operand order is what keeps a deliberately uninitialized field in game/hsfmotion.c unreachable, so the expression's shape is load-bearing rather than stylistic.

evidence.summary: configure.py:648 is Object(Matching, "game/hsfdraw.c"), so the emitted object authenticates this file's source shape, including the expression at src/game/hsfdraw.c:684-685. Reordering the && operands, un-nesting it into separate ifs, or sinking line 684 below the flag test each changes the object.

Line 684 forms texAnimP = &Hu3DTexAnimData[animWorkP->animId] by pointer arithmetic only and never loads through it; the sole dereference, texAnimP->attr, sits on the right of an && testing HU3D_ATTRANIM_ATTR_ANIM2D. SetObjAttrMotion in game/hsfmotion.c clears that bit while leaving animId uninitialized, so the short-circuit is the whole protection. bitMapPtr is protected identically under HU3D_ATTRANIM_ATTR_BMPANIM at line 690.

debt.summary: The reason this operand order matters lives in src/game/hsfmotion.c, not here, and no tool enforces the pairing. The producer-side constraint is hsfmotion-partial-attr-anim-init-guarded-by-short-circuit on the owner main:game/hsfmotion. An agent tidying this expression sees nothing locally wrong.

This owner was created to carry one construct. The rest of the file's semantics, naming and data are not reviewed here; the authenticated status above covers the object's source shape, not a semantic recovery claim over the whole TU.
